guide_enrichment.narrative:
We see the clearest football advantage on BYU’s side of the ball defensively. UCF’s offense has struggled to create efficient production through either the run or the pass, while BYU had allowed only 254.4 total yards and 13.4 points per game through five games. That combination makes sustained UCF drives a legitimate concern, particularly given its difficulty creating scoring opportunities.

BYU’s recent 506-yard performance against Iowa State adds context, but we are not treating one result as proof. Bear Bachmeier had produced 12 total touchdowns against one interception through five games, giving BYU another path to control the game, although the offense used three different starting right tackles across three consecutive contests. For us, the larger point is that the market already appears to account for BYU’s defensive strength and offensive upside. Our numbers do not differ enough from that assessment to create meaningful value, so we are passing.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are focused on UCF’s rushing offense against BYU’s defensive front. UCF’s efficiency on the ground has been poor, while BYU had limited opponents to 80.4 rushing yards per game. If UCF cannot stay efficient on early downs, it may be forced toward a passing matchup that also favors BYU.

That is the central challenge to the UCF side in our model. We need to see whether UCF can generate enough manageable situations and scoring opportunities to keep the margin within range, but the available price does not compensate us for that uncertainty.

recent_game.fact: BYU defeated Iowa State 24-10 on October 9, improving to 5-0 overall and 3-0 in Big 12 play.
BYU outgained Iowa State 506-200, although penalties and red-zone issues kept the game closer.
Bear Bachmeier produced 438 total yards and two touchdowns against Iowa State.
BYU's defense held Iowa State to 200 total yards, the Cyclones' fewest since 2018.

opponent_notes.fact: At the time of this guide, UCF was 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12 with two consecutive losses.
UCF had gained 11 turnovers, the most in the Big 12 at the time of the guide.
UCF led the Big 12 in kickoff-return defense at 13.0 yards allowed per return.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Bear Bachmeier had completed 77 of 116 passes for 1,033 yards, eight touchdowns and one interception through five games, while rushing for 239 yards and four touchdowns.
Bachmeier passed for 329 yards and rushed for 109 yards against Iowa State, becoming the third BYU quarterback with a 300-yard passing and 100-yard rushing game.
Bachmeier's 2026 passing-efficiency rating was 162.2, and he was averaging 254.4 yards of total offense per game.
Treyson Bourguet was listed as Bachmeier's primary backup and had appeared in two games without a start in 2026.

offensive_personnel.fact: BYU's offensive line against Iowa State consisted of Paki Finau at left tackle, Sonny Makasini at left guard, Bruce Mitchell at center, Kyle Sfarcioc at right guard and first-time starter Siosiua Latu-Finau at right tackle.
BYU used three different starting right tackles in consecutive games: Andrew Gentry at Colorado State, freshman Bott Mulitalo at TCU and Siosiua Latu-Finau against Iowa State.
LJ Martin had 344 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 44 carries, an average of 7.8 yards per carry, through four appearances.
Freshman receiver Legend Glasker led BYU with 378 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns and also had 83 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.
Glasker had 99 receiving yards, including a 75-yard touchdown reception, against Iowa State.
USC transfer Walker Lyons started all five games at tight end and caught five passes for 61 yards against Iowa State.
Oregon transfer Roger Saleapaga II caught a career-long 63-yard pass against Iowa State.

defensive_personnel.fact: BYU's defensive starters against Iowa State included Viliami Po'uha and Keanu Tanuvasa on the line; Tausili Akana, Nusi Taumoepeau, Jake Clifton and Cade Uluave in the front seven; and Evan Johnson, Therrian Alexander III, Jayven Williams, Tommy Prassas and Faletau Satuala in the secondary.
Cal transfer Cade Uluave led BYU with 26 tackles through five games and also had 2.5 tackles for loss, a half-sack and one interception.
Defensive end Tausili Akana led BYU with six tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks through five games.
Safety Faletau Satuala had 23 tackles, two tackles for loss, one interception and one pass breakup through five games.
Defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa had 10 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, a half-sack and two pass breakups through five games.

injury_availability.fact: Safety Raider Damuni was injured against Utah Tech and had appeared in only one game through BYU's first five contests; the guide did not provide a return date.
Linebacker Siale Esera was listed as out against Colorado State and TCU; the guide did not explicitly update his availability for later games.
Primary kickoff specialist Brody Laga was injured at Colorado State; the guide did not state a return date.

offensive_context.fact: BYU averaged 433.4 total yards and 34.6 points per game through five games.
BYU averaged 223.8 rushing yards per game, ranking 17th nationally, and had produced 300-yard rushing games against Utah Tech and Colorado State.
BYU converted 54.4 percent of its third downs, ranking seventh nationally.
BYU allowed 1.6 tackles for loss per game, the fewest nationally, and 0.6 sacks per game.
BYU had scored at least five rushing touchdowns in two games, against Utah Tech and Colorado State.
BYU's red-zone scoring rate was 82.6 percent through five games.

defensive_context.fact: BYU allowed 13.4 points per game, ranking ninth nationally, and had held each of its first three Big 12 opponents to 17 points or fewer.
BYU allowed 254.4 total yards per game, ranking eighth nationally and first in the Big 12.
BYU allowed 80.4 rushing yards per game and 174.0 passing yards per game.
BYU had six interceptions through five games, with six different players recording one interception each.
BYU had won 18 consecutive games when forcing at least one turnover, dating to 2024.
Opponents converted 35.4 percent of third downs against BYU but scored on 90 percent of their red-zone possessions.

special_teams.fact: Cannon DeVries had a 100-yard kickoff-return touchdown against Utah Tech and averaged 16.6 yards on seven punt returns.
Fuller Shurtz won the starting punter job after Sam Vander Haar's departure and averaged 45.6 yards on 15 punts, with five punts of at least 50 yards.
Matthias Dunn had made three of four field goals and all 17 extra-point attempts through five games.
BYU averaged 42.0 yards per kickoff return but allowed 28.5 yards per opponent kickoff return.

series_context.fact: BYU defeated UCF 41-21 in their 2025 meeting after overcoming a 14-0 deficit with a 41-7 run; LJ Martin scored three touchdowns and Bear Bachmeier passed for 289 yards.

other_relevant.fact: BYU was 5-0 overall, 3-0 in the Big 12 and ranked No. 8 in both the AP and Coaches polls when this guide was issued.
The UCF game was scheduled for October 24, 2026, on the road, one week after BYU's Notre Dame game.
